questions.problem: Consider the function $f:{R}^{3}\to R$ defined by $f(x)={x}^{T}x.$ What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x?$
questions.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a scalar-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the row vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times n}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{3},$ and

- outputs a scalar $f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3})\in R$ defined by 

$$
f(x)={x}^{T}x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2} & {x}_{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1} & 2{x}_{2} & 2{x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times 3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can also write this as

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=2{x}^{T}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $f,$ defined as 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} \\ x\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the shape of the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x?$
questions.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:R\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a scalar $x$ is the column vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} \\ ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂x}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times 1}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a scalar $x\in R,$ and

- outputs a vector $f(x)\in {R}^{2}.$

Therefore, the total derivative will be a column vector of shape $2\times 1.$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $f:R\to {R}^{4},$ defined by 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 \\ 4 & -5 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x?$
questions.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:R\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a scalar $x$ is the column vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} \\ ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂x}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times 1}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a scalar $x\in R,$ and

- outputs a vector $f(x)\in {R}^{4}$ defined by 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 \\ 4 & -5 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}x+2 \\ 3x \\ 4x-10 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{4}}{∂x}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+2) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(3x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(4x-10) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{4\times 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector-valued function $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ defined by

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]x.
$$

 

What is $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x},$ the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times n}.
$$

In our case, writing out the function $f(x)$ where $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{3}$, we get

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, the total derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{3}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{3}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂{x}_{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{3}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{2}+{x}_{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Since the total derivative is a constant matrix, evaluating it at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ gives the same matrix.
